newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan parliament debates deficit budget.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan parliament debates deficit budget.

text.p: The Moroccan parliament has started debating the 1997/98 budget which favours private enterprise, avoids tax increases and envisages a 12.4 billion dirhams ($1.3 billion) deficit, the official news agency MAP said on Wednesday.
Under the budget, outlined in draft by Finance Minister Mohammed Kabbaj last month, spending will total around 126.7 billion dirhams with revenue at 114.3 billion dirhams.
Kabbaj forecast then that the economy would grow "up to 2.0 to 3.0 percent this year and strong growth in 1998".
MAP on Wednesday quoted opposition party spokesman Fathallah Oualaalou telling parliament that this year would see "negative" economic growth which could not be blamed solely on climate.

The MP, leader of the opposition Socialist Union of People's Forces, said the finance law was a "mirror reflecting the economic crisis affecting the country" as a result of "inappropriate options and bad management".
In 1996 Morocco's GDP growth rate jumped to 11.8 percent after a record 10 million tonnes cereals harvest after a year of severe drought in 1994/95.

MAP quoted Mohamed Kemmou, leader of the pro-government Constitutional Union party, as saying the budget "strives for the promotion of the private sector and reinforcement of competivity, as well as to encourage private initiatives and continued reform in the productive sectors".
The debate was continuing and the budget should be adopted by the 333-seat parliament before the end of June for it to become effective from July 1, the beginning of the fiscal year, officials said.
